items.title: Live: RBA forecasts paint more upbeat picture as interest rates on hold
items.description: The Reserve Bank keeps the cash rate steady at 4.35 per cent in August. Follow live.

items.title: Live: PM rejects suggestion melon comment was a 'classless' reference about women
items.description: Anthony Albanese is resisting opposition calls to apologise to the Japanese PM over hand gestures he made while referring to her gift of crown melons. Follow live.

items.title: Alan Jones trial hears from brother and ex-girlfriend of alleged victim
items.description: The brother of a man accusing Alan Jones of indecent assault has told the court he never saw the radio host act inappropriately towards his brother, and was only told of the allegations after Mr Jones's arrest.

items.title: Bird flu vaccine to be rolled out to vulnerable species in captivity
items.description: A vaccine will be rolled out to protect Australia's native species from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with a focus on birds in captivity.

items.title: NZ PM calls urgent meeting to address 'increased' leadership speculation
items.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon says he has called the in-person meeting of the National Party caucus amid calls from some quarters for a leadership change less than three months before an election.

items.title: 'We deserve to be counted': Gender, sexuality to be asked about in census
items.description: The 2026 census will include questions about sexual orientation and gender identity for the first time to help build a clearer picture of Australia's LGBTQ+ population, and support planning for health and community services.

items.title: 'The right price': How North Korea benefits from Russia alliance
items.description: Almost two weeks ago, what is believed to be a North Korean missile was fired in a Russian attack that killed a Ukrainian family. It could be part of a major escalation in North Korea's involvement in the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Dying woman urges PM to overturn 'cruel' law to save others suffering
items.description: Terminally ill woman Sandra Sarantou is preparing to end her life through voluntary assisted dying (VAD) and is using her final days to call for a legal change to make it easier for others to access VAD.

items.title: More than 132 killed in Colombia after powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake
items.description: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake has shaken parts of Colombia and Ecuador, with reports of significant damage in some areas. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella says at least 132 people are dead in the disaster and that he has assumed leadership of the emergency response. It follows two major quakes in Venezuela in late June which killed more than 5,000 people.

items.title: Why Trump selling early access to his posts is causing controversy
items.description: For up to $US100,000 per month, subscribers can receive the US president's Truth Social posts milliseconds before everyone else. But experts say the bigger question is whether some traders are already getting information much earlier.

items.title: Former Beauty and the Geek contestant pleads not guilty to murder
items.description: A former Beauty and the Geek contestant accused of murdering her partner has denied the allegation and has flagged a potential mental health defence, a court hears.

items.title: NT Police claim they can't trigger curfew in Katherine amid crime fears
items.description: Northern Territory Police have surged resources into the crime-hit town of Katherine, as a federal Labor MP joins calls for a curfew to be triggered as a "circuit breaker".

items.title: How Gianni Infantino's FIFA leadership imploded over two weeks
items.description: The FIFA president has faced more than a fortnight of international turmoil, embroiled in a World Cup sell-off saga that sparked loss of confidence in his leadership.

items.title: The absurdity of Aussie rules football inspires new comedy video game
items.description: Mixing 1990s-era gameplay aesthetics with silly power-ups, Pro Jank Footy has fun with a national obsession.

items.title: Quiz: Does Australia have more baristas or personal trainers?
items.description: Today's More or Less quiz challenges you to rank different occupations by how many people do them.

items.title: Perhaps the answer to my dating woes is to simply tell people who I am
items.description: Every time I rejoin a dating site, I am faced with the dilemma of whether to include my disability in my profile, or self-censor in a bid to follow the rules of what is "normal".

items.title: 'They will be taken over': Warning for Philippines as dispute with China erupts
items.description: Foreign Correspondent journeys to one of the world's most contested islands where China's shadowy 'maritime militia' lurks just off the coast.

items.title: Children encountering extremism at 'disturbing' rate, inquiry told
items.description: Children at an increasingly young age are engaging with violent extremist material at a "disturbing" rate, Australia's counter-terrorism coordinator says.

items.title: This international student helped Bondi attack victims. It could cost him
items.description: Abdullah Ashraf, a law student from Pakistan, had his student visa lapse while on compassionate leave from his studies in the aftermath of the Bondi Beach terror attack.

items.title: The medics offering healthcare to homeless people 'no questions asked'
items.description: A new service is opening in Canberra to provide medical care to those in insecure housing situations, but the team behind it also wants to develop relationships with people who have grown distrustful of the healthcare system.

items.title: 'Never forgotten where he's from': Outback community pride for Crows legend
items.description: Taylor 'Tex' Walker has etched himself into the Adelaide Crows' history books, but his hometown of Broken Hill holds so much admiration for his career.

items.title: Victoria's work-from-home laws delayed until July 2027
items.description: Premier Ben Carroll has promised to reset his relationship with Victorian businesses, and says he is open to "common-sense" amendments to the proposed work-from-home legislation.

items.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez open to presidential run, announces she will freeze eggs
items.description: The 36-year-old said she felt "empowered" by her decision, while adding that it came with political risk.

items.title: US had hottest month on record in July, England's drought worsens
items.description: July 2026 was the hottest month ever in the United States, whilst almost three-quarters of England is now in drought.

items.title: Why did Israel reject Donald Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza?
items.description: Israel's rejection of Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan is not a surprise. Here's why and how politics plays into it ahead of an Israeli election.
